description: The Office of Congressman Robert Garcia (CA-42) is currently hiring for a Paid Part-Time Press Intern position (asap - Spring 2025) to work in the Washington, D.C. office. The Press Intern works closely with the communications team.
responsibilities: Drafting press releases and other written materials.
Clipping committee remarks and cable hits.
qualifications: Must be able to work in a fast-paced environment.
Previous experience in communications with attention to detail and deadlines.
how_to_apply: Interested applicants should send a one page resume, 1 sample press release, and 2 relevant sample tweets to sara.guerrero@mail.house.gov and emily.kassnermarks@mail.house.gov with "INTERN APP: Full Name" in the subject line. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.
equal_opportunity: The office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, national origin, disability, military status, age, marital status, or parental status.

description: Congressman French Hill (AR02) seeks interns to serve in his offices in Washington, D.C., and Arkansas. Interns will work in a fast-paced office, gaining valuable exposure and knowledge of the legislative process and the U.S. Congress. Standard internships take place as follows: Spring: January through May; Summer: May through August; Fall: September through November. Internships outside of this schedule may be offered on a case-by-case basis. Paid and unpaid internships are available.
responsibilities: Interacting with Arkansans and other visitors
Assisting Arkansans with matters before the federal government
qualifications: Excellent written and oral communication skills
Working knowledge of current events and policy topics
Willingness to assist with daily office tasks
Social media and other communications experience (a plus)
Ability to listen to and take direction
Willingness to work both independently and as part of a team
how_to_apply: Interested individuals should send a resume and cover letter to ar02.applications@mail.house.gov. For more information, please call (501) 324-5941 or (202) 225-2506 and ask for the Intern Coordinator.

description: The Committee on House Administration Republican Office seeks energetic and self-motivated individuals with an interest in government and public policy, to apply for its paid, full-time internship program. The Committee on House Administration maintains jurisdiction of federal election policy and manages the day-to-day operations of the House of Representatives with oversight of several offices within the Capitol Complex, including the Chief Administrative Officer, Architect of the Capitol, Clerk of the House, House Inspector General, Sergeant at Arms, U.S. Capitol Police, and other legislative branch entities like the Library of Congress, Government Publishing Office, and the Smithsonian Institution. Working closely with Committee staff, interns will have the opportunity to gain first-hand knowledge of the inner-workings of a congressional committee and learn about the day-to-day administrative operations of the House of Representatives. Interns are responsible for assisting Committee staff with official proceedings (hearings/markups), oversight, research, assisting with phones, and providing support to all Committee staff.
responsibilities: Assisting Committee staff with official proceedings (hearings/markups)
Providing support to all Committee staff
Reaching out to agencies and other congressional offices
qualifications: Interest in government and public policy
how_to_apply: Please send a resume, cover letter, and availability to CHAInternGOP@mail.house.gov.

description: The Washington DC office of Congressman Pat Fallon is looking for spring 2025 interns. In the Washington, DC office, internships run throughout the fall, spring, or summer semesters for college students. The hours are flexible to accommodate students' hectic course schedules, but generally run 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. when Congress is in session, and 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. when not in session. In Washington, DC, interns' responsibilities will vary. They will be asked to answer phones, run errands, research legislation for the Member and legislative staff, attend hearings and briefings, and answer constituent letters on various issues before the House. As a result, interns learn about the legislative process and the many other functions of a congressional office.
responsibilities: Research legislation for the Member and legislative staff
Answer constituent letters on various issues before the House
qualifications: Available during fall, spring, or summer semesters
Flexible schedule to accommodate course schedules, generally 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. when Congress is in session and 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. when not in session
how_to_apply: Visit the "Internships" page on Congressman Fallon's website and complete the application: https://fallon.house.gov/services/internships.htm
